stories.headline: Tanker hit off Qatar as mediators push US-Iran draft; Vance blames war for midterm loss

key_facts.fact: A tanker was struck by two unidentified projectiles about 50 nautical miles north of Madinat ash Shamal, Qatar, at 23:20 UTC on Wednesday, Nov. 4, according to UK Maritime Trade Operations; crew status and damage were unknown.
key_facts.excerpt: A tanker was struck by two unidentified projectiles about 50 nautical miles north of Madinat ash Shamal, Qatar... The incident took place at 11.20pm UTC on Wednesday... The status of the crew, the extent of the damage and any environmental impact are not yet known.

key_facts.fact: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two tankers and a tugboat caught fire overnight on an 'unauthorised' route, and that another tanker hit a mine early Thursday, warning that the Strait of Hormuz is 'unsafe and closed' to ships transiting without coordination. These are Iranian claims.
key_facts.excerpt: A tanker caught fire after hitting a naval mine east of the Strait of Hormuz early on Thursday... The Guards warned shipowners that the Strait of Hormuz was 'unsafe and closed' to vessels attempting to transit without coordination.

key_facts.fact: Vice President JD Vance wrote that 'the reason we lost is the war'; Trump called that 'largely true because it drove gasoline up a little bit' but added 'if I had to do it again, I'd do it again.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'The reason we lost,' Vance said of the midterm elections in a lengthy social media post, 'is the war.' ... 'It's largely true because it drove gasoline up a little bit,' Trump said... 'At the same time, if I had to do it again, I'd do it again.'

key_facts.fact: Qatari mediators are seeking US and Iranian backing for a draft agreement with a three-day sequence of confidence-building steps that could restart direct talks within days; Iran demands an end to the US naval blockade, sanctions relief and release of frozen funds before reopening Hormuz.
key_facts.excerpt: Qatari mediators are trying to win US and Iranian backing for a draft agreement meant to head off renewed fighting and possibly restart direct talks 'within days'. Earlier reporting said the draft outlines a three-day sequence of confidence-building steps. Iran has demanded an end to the US naval blockade, sanctions relief and release of frozen funds before it will reopen Hormuz.

key_facts.fact: Oman said its foreign minister and Iran's Abbas Araghchi discussed on Thursday joint technical mechanisms for Hormuz traffic 'in a manner that would end the state of war.'
key_facts.excerpt: both men 'stressed the importance of moving from the stage of de-escalating tensions to one of establishing sustainable understandings based on practical arrangements to ensure the safety of maritime routes and joint technical mechanisms ... in a manner that would end the state of war and prevent renewed confrontations in the region.'

key_facts.fact: US officials told Axios the military is finishing preparations for a possible resumption of major combat, including sending more assets to the region; the preparations are not an order to attack.
key_facts.excerpt: US officials told Axios the military is finishing preparations for a possible resumption of major combat operations, including sending more assets to the region. Preparations are not an order.

key_facts.fact: The Financial Times reported on Thursday that Russia agreed to supply Iran with 90 helicopter-mounted launchers for precision-guided missiles widely used by Russian forces in Ukraine.
key_facts.excerpt: Russia agreed to supply Iran with 90 helicopter-mounted launchers for precision-guided missiles widely used by Russian forces in Ukraine, the Financial Times reported on Thursday.

key_facts.fact: Trump told ABC News on Thursday he intends to keep Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth despite criticism of his leadership after the Iran war and the midterm losses: 'I have every intention to keep him.'
key_facts.excerpt: US President Donald Trump said on Thursday he intended to retain Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth despite criticism of his leadership following the Iran war and Republicans' midterm election losses. 'I have every intention to keep him,' Trump told ABC News.

stories.headline: Saudi coalition downs Houthi missile aimed at Medina; WSJ says Houthis demand $51B to end war

key_facts.fact: The Saudi-led coalition said on Thursday, Nov. 5, that its air defenses intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by the Houthis toward the Medina region.
key_facts.excerpt: The Saudi-led coalition said on Thursday that its air defenses intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by Houthi forces toward the Medina region.

key_facts.fact: Saudi Civil Defence issued an all-clear for Yanbu, in the Medina region, and warned that filming or sharing information about interceptions or impact sites could lead to legal action.
key_facts.excerpt: Saudi Arabia's Civil Defence said the danger has passed in Yanbu Governorate... The authority also warned that filming, publishing or sharing information about the interception of missiles and drones, or the sites where they fall, could lead to legal action.

key_facts.fact: The Wall Street Journal reported that the Houthis are demanding $51 billion from Saudi Arabia plus official recognition as Yemen's rulers as baseline conditions for ending the war; other amounts have been discussed, with a deal's price still in the tens of billions.
key_facts.excerpt: Yemen's Houthis are demanding $51 billion from Saudi Arabia as compensation for years of airstrikes and blockade, along with official recognition of Ansarallah as Yemen's rulers... Other amounts have since been discussed, but the price of a deal remains in the tens of billions.

key_facts.fact: Per the same report, Riyadh made contact after Houthi attacks on Aramco facilities, the East-West Pipeline, King Khalid International Airport and Red Sea tankers, and after Houthi territorial gains around Bab el-Mandeb.
key_facts.excerpt: Riyadh reportedly made contact after Houthi attacks on Aramco facilities, the East-West Pipeline, King Khalid International Airport and Red Sea tankers, as well as territorial gains around Bab el-Mandeb.

key_facts.fact: CBS News reports Houthi missile strikes on Saudi airports have killed at least 20 people; Iran's foreign ministry on Thursday again denied that Iranian military experts are in Yemen, after EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas called on Iran to stop supporting the group.
key_facts.excerpt: Since then, Houthi missile strikes on Saudi Arabian airports have killed at least 20 people... Baqaei called the latest accusation ... 'baseless,' and said Iran 'strongly denied claims that Iranian military experts were present in Yemen.'

stories.headline: Bank of England raises rates to 4% in 8-1 vote, sees inflation near 5% on energy shock

key_facts.fact: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee voted 8-1 to raise Bank Rate by 0.25 percentage points to 4%, with one member voting for a half-point rise to 4.25%; the decision was published Nov. 5.
key_facts.excerpt: At its meeting ending on 4 November 2026, the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) voted by a majority of 8-1 to increase Bank Rate by 0.25 percentage points, to 4%. One member voted to increase Bank Rate by 0.5 percentage points, to 4.25%.

key_facts.fact: UK CPI inflation reached 3.5% in September and the Bank now expects it to rise to around 5% by the middle of next year before falling.
key_facts.excerpt: UK CPI inflation increased to 3.5% in September. It is now expected to rise to around 5% by the middle of next year.

key_facts.fact: The Bank said the Middle East conflict is in its ninth month and that pipeline inflation pressure now warrants a hike, though it sees 'limited evidence' of knock-on effects on other prices and wages.
key_facts.excerpt: there remains limited evidence of knock-on effects on other prices and wages. However, the degree of inflationary pressure in the pipeline is now sufficient to warrant an increase in Bank Rate.

key_facts.fact: The minutes put Brent at an average of $108 a barrel over the 15 UK working days to Oct. 27, 38% above the level at the July report; UK natural gas averaged 216 pence per therm, 81% higher.
key_facts.excerpt: The front-month Brent crude oil futures contract and the UK front-month natural gas futures contract averaged $108 per barrel and 216 pence per therm, respectively, over the 15 UK working days ending 27 October. These were 38% and 81% higher than at the time of the July Monetary Policy Report.

key_facts.fact: Reuters noted before the decision that a hike would be the Bank's first in more than three years, joining most G10 peers, with around 100 basis points of tightening priced in by the end of next year.
key_facts.excerpt: The Bank of England decides interest rates on Thursday, and is expected to finally join most of its G10 peers in raising borrowing costs... It would be the Bank's first hike in more than three years... Around 100 basis points of tightening is priced in by the end of next year.

stories.headline: Dow jumps 3%, best day since April 2025, as oil plunges 8% on bets the Iran war will end

key_facts.fact: On Wednesday, Nov. 4, the Dow rose 1,569.40 points, or 3.03%, to 53,356.12, its best day since April 9, 2025; the S&P 500 gained 1.58% to 7,688.62 and the Nasdaq Composite 1.44% to 25,736.51.
key_facts.excerpt: The Dow Jones Industrial Average jumped 1,569.40 points, or 3.03%, to close at 53,356.12... posted its best day since April 9, 2025... The S&P 500 gained 1.58% to end at 7,688.62, while the Nasdaq Composite jumped 1.44% to 25,736.51.

key_facts.fact: Brent and WTI fell about 8% on Wednesday; Reuters said Brent was down nearly 20% on the week so far and on course for the biggest weekly decline since April 2020.
key_facts.excerpt: the plunge in oil prices on Wednesday puts Brent and WTI crude futures on course for their biggest weekly decline since the white heat of the global pandemic in April 2020. Brent is down nearly 20% so far this week, WTI is down 15%.

key_facts.fact: On Thursday, Brent recovered to $96.15, up 1.6%, while Eurasia Group put the odds of renewed US strikes on Iran at 60%, down from 65%, and cut the odds of a deal to 10% from 20%.
key_facts.excerpt: Brent futures were up $1.53, or 1.6%, at $96.15 a barrel... Eurasia Group lowered its estimate for the chance of renewed US strikes on Iran to 60% from 65%, but also cut the probability of a deal to 10% from 20%.

key_facts.fact: JPMorgan estimates the oil market returned to a surplus of 1.1 million barrels per day in September, widening to 1.4 million in October, as Gulf supply resumed.
key_facts.excerpt: JPMorgan estimates the market returned to a surplus of 1.1 million barrels per day in September, widening to 1.4 million bpd in October.

key_facts.fact: The 10-year Treasury yield fell 7.4 basis points to 4.888%, yet markets still priced an 81% chance of a 25-basis-point Fed rate hike at the Dec. 8-9 meeting; the 10-year breakeven inflation rate fell to 2.248%.
key_facts.excerpt: The 10-year T-note yield fell -7.4 bp to 4.888%... The markets are now pricing in an 81% chance of a +25 bp rate hike at the FOMC's next meeting on December 8-9.

key_facts.fact: ADP reported that private employers added 86,000 jobs in October, above estimates.
key_facts.excerpt: The payrolls processing firm said companies added 86,000 jobs during the month, the same as the downwardly revised total for September and slightly ahead of the Dow Jones estimate for 75,000.

key_facts.fact: Energy was the worst S&P 500 sector, down 4.8%, while consumer discretionary rose about 4.3%; Microsoft gained 6.7% and Amazon 6.1%, while Hut 8 fell 23%, IREN 11% and Core Scientific 10% on fears of tighter AI regulation.
key_facts.excerpt: Microsoft rose 6.7%, Amazon.com added 6.1%... Hut 8 down 23%, IREN off 11%, Core Scientific falling 10%... consumer discretionary jumping 4.3% and energy falling 4.8%.

key_facts.fact: Health insurer and hospital shares rallied on speculation that a Democratic Congress could roll back Medicaid cuts, with Centene up more than 12% and HCA Healthcare more than 10%.
key_facts.excerpt: Health insurance stocks moved higher Wednesday on speculation that a Democratic controlled Congress could roll back the Medicaid cuts... Centene (CNC) closed up more than +12%, and HCA Healthcare (HCA) and United Health Services (UHS) closed up more than +10%.

stories.headline: US job cuts hit 43,994 in October; AI cited for just 1,265 as economy overtakes it as top reason

key_facts.fact: US employers announced 43,994 job cuts in October, up 2% from September, down 71% from 153,074 a year earlier, and the lowest October total since 2023, Challenger, Gray & Christmas reported Nov. 5.
key_facts.excerpt: U.S.-based employers announced 43,994 job cuts in October, up 2% from the 43,281 cuts announced in September. It is down 71% from the 153,074 job cuts announced in October 2025.

key_facts.fact: AI was cited for 1,265 cuts in October, its lowest monthly total this year; it has been cited for 121,401 cuts in 2026, about 20% of the total, and 193,226 since Challenger began tracking it in 2023.
key_facts.excerpt: AI was cited for 1,265 cuts in October, its lowest monthly total this year. AI has been cited in 121,401 job cut announcements so far in 2026, approximately 20% of all cuts. Since 2023... it has been cited in 193,226 job cuts.

key_facts.fact: Market/economic conditions led October's reasons with 16,407 cuts, or 37%, and with 130,531 cuts this year has overtaken AI as 2026's leading reason.
key_facts.excerpt: Market/Economic Conditions led all reasons in October for the second consecutive month, cited for 16,407 cuts, or 37% of the total. With 130,531 cuts so far this year, Market/Economic Conditions has overtaken Artificial Intelligence (AI) as the leading reason for job cuts in 2026.

key_facts.fact: Year-to-date cuts total 617,189, down 44%; technology still leads with 171,501, up 21%, even though its 5,576 October cuts were its lowest monthly total of the year.
key_facts.excerpt: Through October, employers have announced 617,189 job cuts, down 44%... Technology announced 5,576 cuts in October, its lowest monthly total of the year. Even so, the sector leads all industries with 171,501 cuts through October, up 21%.

key_facts.fact: Microsoft's voluntary exit offers to 60,000 employees in October are not counted in the total; Andy Challenger said such offers 'tend to signal more layoffs to come.'
key_facts.excerpt: Microsoft also announced voluntary exit offers (VEOs) to 60,000 employees in October... the offers are not included in October's total. 'These offers tend to signal more layoffs to come.'

key_facts.fact: Seasonal hiring plans reached 470,400 through October, up 26%, led by Amazon's 300,000, the largest single seasonal announcement Challenger has tracked; only five companies have announced seasonal hiring, versus 11 at this point last year.
key_facts.excerpt: 470,400 seasonal hiring plans through October... up 26%... Amazon led seasonal announcements with plans to hire 300,000 workers... It is the largest single seasonal hiring announcement Challenger has tracked... five companies have announced seasonal hiring so far this year, compared with 11 at this point last year.

stories.headline: US, Ukraine and Europeans meet in Brussels ahead of Nov. 10-11 Abu Dhabi talks with Russia

key_facts.fact: The European Commission hosted talks on Nov. 4 with the US, Ukraine, NATO and several European countries to coordinate positions before trilateral talks among Ukraine, Russia and the US scheduled for Nov. 10-11 in Abu Dhabi.
key_facts.excerpt: The European Commission hosted talks on Ukraine in Brussels on Nov. 4, bringing together representatives from the U.S., Ukraine, NATO, and several European countries... ahead of the next round of trilateral talks between Ukraine, Russia, and the U.S., scheduled for Nov. 10-11 in Abu Dhabi.

key_facts.fact: Zelensky held a 90-minute call on Nov. 4 with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner covering air defense munitions, the US-Ukraine drone deal and post-war guarantees, saying 'We need interceptors for Patriot systems' and that guarantees 'must be truly ironclad.'
key_facts.excerpt: Zelensky said he 'had a very detailed conversation' with Witkoff and Kushner that lasted an hour and a half. Among the primary topics were air defense munitions, the U.S.-Ukraine Drone Deal, and post-war security guarantees.

key_facts.fact: The Abu Dhabi round will be at team level, with technical negotiations that could lead to a summit of Zelensky, Putin and Trump.
key_facts.excerpt: The Abu Dhabi talks will be held at the team level, with delegates from all three countries holding technical negotiations that could lead to a leader-level summit involving Zelensky, Russian President Vladimir Putin, and U.S. President Donald Trump.

key_facts.fact: The trilateral meeting was initially expected in October, but the Kremlin declined to participate after agreeing in principle; Moscow continues to demand that Ukraine cede Donbas.
key_facts.excerpt: The trilateral meeting with Russia was initially expected to take place in October... The visits resulted in an agreement in principle to hold negotiations, but the Kremlin later declined to participate... while continuing to demand that Ukraine cede Donbas.

key_facts.fact: China's foreign ministry said Wednesday that Beijing is 'in communication with relevant parties' about a possible Trump-Xi-Putin meeting at the APEC leaders' gathering in Shenzhen later this month; no agenda has been announced.
key_facts.excerpt: Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said Wednesday that Beijing was 'in communication with relevant parties regarding a meeting between the three heads of state,' although no agenda has been announced.

key_facts.fact: Overnight into Nov. 5, Russia launched two guided missiles and 128 long-range drones, of which Ukraine said it intercepted 105 drones; Russian attacks killed nine people and injured 19 over the past day, local authorities said.
key_facts.excerpt: Russian forces launched two guided missiles from the Black Sea and 128 long-range attack drones at Ukraine overnight on Nov. 5... Ukrainian air defenses had intercepted 105 Russian drones... killed nine people and injured 19 others.

key_facts.fact: The confirmed toll from the Nov. 2 Russian aerial-bomb strike on Komyshuvakha, in Zaporizhzhia Oblast, reached 42 dead with 33 still missing as of Nov. 5, police said.
key_facts.excerpt: The bodies of 42 Ukrainians have been recovered from the rubble in the village of Komyshuvakha in Zaporizhzhia Oblast, with 33 more people still missing as of Nov. 5, three days after Russian forces attacked the settlement with heavy aerial bombs.

stories.headline: Boehringer licenses six Chinese cancer programs from Sino Biopharm in deal worth up to $7B

key_facts.fact: Boehringer Ingelheim signed a licensing and development agreement with Sino Biopharmaceutical covering six preclinical cancer programs: antibody-drug conjugates and T-cell engagers.
key_facts.excerpt: The German pharmaceutical company has signed a comprehensive licensing and development agreement with Sino Biopharmaceutical (SBP Group) covering six preclinical cancer therapy programs. The deal focuses on two drug classes... antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) and T-cell engagers.

key_facts.fact: Sino Biopharm receives $358 million in upfront and near-term payments, with up to $7 billion more in milestones plus tiered royalties; the milestone sum is contingent, not a guaranteed payment.
key_facts.excerpt: SBP will initially receive $358 million in upfront and near-term payments. The agreement also includes potential milestone payments of up to $7 billion and tiered royalties... the $7 billion is neither a purchase price nor a guaranteed payment.

key_facts.fact: Sino Biopharm leads early development, and Boehringer can exercise options after clinical milestones: rights to four programs exclude mainland China, Hong Kong and Macau, while rights to two could be worldwide.
key_facts.excerpt: Sino will lead early development. Boehringer can exercise options after clinical milestones. Boehringer's potential rights to four programs exclude mainland China, Hong Kong, and Macau. Rights to the other two could be worldwide.

key_facts.fact: Five candidates come from Shanghai-based LaNova Medicines and one from Beijing Tide Pharmaceutical, both Sino Biopharm subsidiaries; targets and indications have not been disclosed.
key_facts.excerpt: Five of the six preclinical programs originate from Shanghai-based LaNova Medicines, a wholly owned subsidiary of SBP. The sixth comes from Beijing Tide Pharmaceutical... The companies have not yet disclosed further details about the specific targets, indications or development stages.

key_facts.fact: The deal follows Boehringer's opening of a China R&D center in Shanghai on Oct. 12.
key_facts.excerpt: On October 12, Boehringer opened a new China Research and Development Center in Shanghai.
